requirements.positive: one owner acquires fence and advances one pending row
requirements.adversarial: two processes synchronize lookup/send, lease expires, old PID is reused
requirements.invariant: only the highest live fence token may send or mutate
requirements.oracle: exactly one send authority; every stale-fence mutation is rejected
requirements.false_positive: shared mocks serialize contenders and hide the race
requirements.false_negative: scheduler delay is mistaken for fencing

requirements.positive: authorized key signs every canonical receipt field
requirements.negative: signature or required binding is absent
requirements.adversarial: mutate issuer, version, project, operation, request digest, event, outcome, key, or epoch one at a time
requirements.invariant: ACKED requires a fully verified request-bound receipt
requirements.oracle: valid control ACKs; every field mutation leaves a non-ACK state
requirements.false_positive: test signs mutated content with the trusted key

requirements.positive: each allowed transition reaches its declared successor
requirements.adversarial: crash immediately before and after every state write and network action
requirements.invariant: ambiguity is durable and never represented as success or silently retransmitted
requirements.oracle: observed trace is accepted by the frozen state graph and has no unguarded send
requirements.false_positive: crash hook fires outside the named boundary
requirements.false_negative: equivalent idempotent replay is rejected by an underspecified graph

requirements.positive: complete bound receipt is accepted atomically
requirements.negative: truncated JSON, missing field, wrong type, duplicate key, or oversize
requirements.adversarial: cross-project, cross-operation, cross-digest, event substitution, and corrupted stored JSON
requirements.invariant: invalid receipt causes no ACK and no destructive state change
requirements.oracle: false_ack_count is zero and each vector has the frozen reason code
requirements.false_positive: parser rejects before semantic binding is exercised
requirements.false_negative: valid boundary-size receipt omitted from control set

requirements.negative: I/O error or kill interrupts ACK transaction
requirements.adversarial: kill at SQLite begin, WAL write, fsync, commit, checkpoint, and stale-owner ACK
requirements.invariant: restart yields prior reconcilable state or one fully durable verified ACK
requirements.oracle: integrity_check=ok and state is exactly pre-ACK or verified ACK
requirements.false_positive: process kill does not reach storage boundary
requirements.false_negative: WAL recovery is observed before SQLite completes normal recovery

requirements.negative: payload digest mismatch or invalid schema version
requirements.adversarial: page bit flip, truncation, damaged WAL, invalid JSON, receipt corruption, and partial backup
requirements.invariant: corruption never causes send, ACK, deletion, or silent repair
requirements.oracle: zero network actions and forensic bytes preserved before bounded quarantine
requirements.false_negative: whole-database refusal is mislabeled as minimal quarantine failure

requirements.positive: capacity is available at every durability boundary
requirements.negative: SQLite FULL or IOERR during enqueue, send-state, or ACK
requirements.adversarial: ENOSPC, inode exhaustion, read-only remount, permission loss, and log amplification
requirements.invariant: no send precedes durable pre-send state and no ACK precedes durable receipt
requirements.oracle: no unjournaled effects or false success; restoration produces deterministic recovery
requirements.false_positive: mocked error bypasses SQLite transaction path
requirements.false_negative: expected platform-specific error code is overconstrained

requirements.positive: authorized operator inspects then dispositions a stale row
requirements.negative: age threshold alone attempts resend, success, or deletion
requirements.adversarial: wall-clock rollback/jump, policy version change, delayed receipt, and abandoned project
requirements.invariant: age alone never determines commit status or destructive action
requirements.oracle: zero age-triggered network/destructive actions; disposition is authorized and durable
requirements.false_positive: fixture uses monotonic time while product uses wall clock
requirements.false_negative: read-only stale classification is mistaken for disposition

requirements.positive: declared supported topology has one fenced advancer
requirements.adversarial: two hosts, partition, failover, reboot, asymmetric Station access, and stale replica
requirements.invariant: multi-host recovery is fenced by qualified authority or fails closed before send
requirements.oracle: one advancement per operation or explicit unsupported-topology refusal
requirements.false_positive: hosts accidentally share an in-process lock
requirements.false_negative: safe loss of liveness is classified as safety failure

requirements.positive: each durable transition emits one bounded correlated observation
requirements.negative: missing, duplicate, secret-bearing, or unbounded-label observation
requirements.adversarial: exporter outage, hostile receipt/message labels, clock skew, and alert storm
requirements.invariant: telemetry reconciles to state without secrets or unbounded cardinality
requirements.oracle: recomputed counters equal durable journal; forbidden data absent; required alert fires
requirements.false_positive: oracle reads the same derived counter as exporter
requirements.false_negative: permitted hashed correlation IDs flagged as secrets

requirements.positive: declared compatible sender and Station negotiate before mutation
requirements.negative: unknown major version or safety-removing downgrade
requirements.adversarial: old/new pairs across send, lookup, restart, upgrade, and rollback
requirements.invariant: unknown/incompatible versions create no external effect
requirements.oracle: supported pairs match registry; unsupported pairs have zero mutations/effects
requirements.false_positive: both sides import one schema implementation
requirements.false_negative: optional additive fields treated as major incompatibility

requirements.positive: authoritative lookup returns bound presence or qualified absence
requirements.adversarial: leader loss, partition, DR, stale cache, lost index with retained event
requirements.invariant: absence is authority-qualified and never directly authorizes duplicate effect
requirements.oracle: non-authoritative/indeterminate lookup produces no repost and later converges
requirements.false_negative: qualified durable absence cannot progress under any policy

requirements.positive: tombstone preserves uniqueness through replay horizon
requirements.negative: receipt/idempotency deletion makes old operation new
requirements.adversarial: race GC with lookup, restore old client backup, shrink policy, and storage pressure
requirements.invariant: GC never erases uniqueness while retry remains possible
requirements.oracle: restored clients cannot create a second event and storage bound holds
requirements.false_positive: test duration never crosses actual retention boundary
requirements.false_negative: legal deletion refusal is confused with uniqueness failure

requirements.positive: consumer applies stable effect ID transactionally or idempotently
requirements.negative: consumer effects then crashes before offset/ACK
requirements.adversarial: duplicate delivery, reorder, restore, non-idempotent connector, and partial fanout
requirements.invariant: published at-most-once claim names the exact effect boundary; unknown is indeterminate
requirements.oracle: model and ledger satisfy the frozen property within the declared boundary
requirements.false_negative: duplicate delivery with deduplicated effect counted twice
